root_cause.text: The vmemmap_shift computed from the alignment of start_pfn and last_pfn is not clamped to MAX_FOLIO_ORDER, allowing an unsupported compound page order that triggers a WARN and returns -EINVAL from memremap_pages().
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "However, this value is not clamped to MAX_FOLIO_ORDER, so a sufficiently aligned range ... can produce a shift larger than what memremap_pages() accepts". The patch adds `pgmap->vmemmap_shift = min(count_trailing_zeros(...), MAX_FOLIO_ORDER);` and notes that the MAX_FOLIO_ORDER check was added by commit 646b67d57589.

candidates.rationale: Copies user-controlled start_pfn and last_pfn without validating their alignment or order, allowing arbitrary values to reach the vmemmap_shift computation.
Checks only that last_pfn > start_pfn but does not enforce alignment constraints or limit the resulting page order, missing the necessary clamp.
Uses the unvalidated start_pfn to set the physical start address, which influences the alignment used to compute vmemmap_shift.
Uses the unvalidated last_pfn to set the physical end address, which together with the start determines the trailing zeros count for vmemmap_shift.
Directly assigns the vmemmap_shift without clamping to MAX_FOLIO_ORDER, allowing an unsupported compound page order that triggers a WARN and -EINVAL in memremap_pages().

Logs the unclamped vmemmap_shift, but more importantly the statement exists and is part of the same code flow; it does not cause the vulnerability itself but shows the order is printed without checking.
Checks the return value of devm_memremap_pages, which is where the WARN and -EINVAL are triggered due to the unclamped vmemmap_shift; this line is part of the error handling path.
Defines the start_pfn field in the user-facing structure; user-space can set this to arbitrary values, directly enabling the vulnerable computation.
Defines the last_pfn field in the user-facing structure; together with start_pfn, its trailing zeros determine vmemmap_shift without restriction.
